criteria.header_validated: Beyond the magic prefix, confirm each binary format fixed header: lengths that fit inside the file, positive dimensions and counts, and legal version and type codes. Checksums, decompression, and pixel decoding stay out. Cut-off or scrambled files die at build with an exact signature error rather than shipping to browsers as damaged bytes.
criteria.magic_only: Confirm just the opening magic bytes of each binary format. The adapter remains minimal; files pairing a good prefix with a broken body still emit and serve, and browsers turn them away. Build detection still catches blunt mismatches like a text file wearing a .png name.

binary_signature_depth.instructions: Determine binary asset signature depth: opening magic bytes alone, or magic together with fixed header structure minus checksums and decoding. Reason from common with topics.binary_signature_depth.

criteria.json_bytes: Take every well-formed UTF-8 file as .json and serve it under application/json. Browsers own parsing; a broken document ships truthfully as data instead of dying at build.
criteria.json_must_parse: Turn away any .json asset whose bytes fail JSON parsing, reading the grammar as the format signature. Broken documents die at build; each served .json asset parses.
criteria.review_needed: This material cannot settle .json policy, or neither policy respects the contracts.

json_policy.instructions: Determine whether .json assets must parse during the build or may serve arbitrary UTF-8 text. Reason from common with topics.json_policy.

criteria.caller_only: Settle each name inside the manifest of the project holding the calling source. Dependency assets remain reachable solely via callee code handing back html::url values; raw names never traverse project edges. A single manifest per call excludes precedence and collision rules.

criteria.root_union: Settle each name across the root manifest plus all transitive dependency manifests under a fixed precedence order and a twice-declared conflict rule. Raw names traverse edges; sharing skips wrapper functions.

ownership_scope.instructions: Determine the manifest set behind an asset::url name: the caller project manifest alone, or root plus transitive dependency manifests with precedence. Reason from common with topics.ownership_scope.

criteria.single_missing: Mark all unresolvable names with the lone reason missing. Callers match once; the failure whereabouts stays hidden.
criteria.specific_taxonomy: Mark names known nowhere as missing and names housed only in another project as unowned. Callers separate typos from boundary mistakes.

reason_vocabulary.instructions: Determine invalid_url reasons for unresolvable asset names: a lone reason for all cases, or separate reasons for unknown versus foreign names. Reason from common with topics.reason_vocabulary.

fixed_constraints: Native-equivalence rule: Can operations compile into matching native JavaScript/Bun operations, admitting adapters purely for Can contract and immutability enforcement. External users number zero, hence historic syntax, ABI, layouts, and goldens merit zero compatibility spend; favor compiler spareness wherever meaning endures.

P11 charter: the distribution carries upstream HTMX 2.0.10 bytes proven against sha384-H5SrcfygHmAuTDZphMHqBJLc3FhssKjG7w/CeCpFReSfwBWDTKpkzPP8c+cLsK+V, served from /__can/assets/htmx-2.0.10.min.js under the JavaScript media type with immutable cache headers plus an ETag. htmx-config pins allowEval=false, allowScriptTags=false, selfRequestsOnly=true, mapping 204 onto no-swap, 422 onto swap, and remaining errors onto no-swap. Project routes never eclipse /__can/.

Project assets enter as manifest build inputs, hashed by the compiler, served from /__can/project/<digest>/<name> through native Bun.file under fixed media types, nosniff, ETag, and immutable caching. Admitted suffixes run .css .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .ico .woff .woff2 .txt .json .csv. JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, SVG/XML, WebAssembly, source maps, and unfamiliar suffixes die, as do mismatched signatures. Digests render sha256 hex across the bytes.

Catalogue charter: asset::url(static str name) yields html::url, emits html::invalid_url, executes genuinely under assertions, and settles a declared asset name during compilation. invalid_url already speaks syntax, scheme, authority, and same_origin. Route mounts already demand static string literals when checked, leaving malformed literals to the checker instead of runtime.

Pipeline contour: per-project manifests map asset names toward confined normalized paths; project snapshotting hashes bytes and aborts the build over unreadable files, unsafe names, spurned suffixes, or poor signatures. The checker settles each static name against manifest ownership and embeds either the derived URL or a domain-failure reason; runtime mints html::url provenance or relays the reason. Served files descend solely from a compiler-built table; reserved routes outrank application routing.
common.purpose: Advise on Can, an immutable compiled language, from this request evidence alone. Outside research, implementation work, and explanatory answer prose are all out of scope. Whenever candidates stay indistinguishable, the explicit uncertainty option fits.

binary_signature_depth.facts: Admitted binary formats PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, AVIF, ICO, WOFF, and WOFF2 each publish a magic prefix alongside fixed header fields. Complete decodes (CRC verification, decompression, pixel extraction) would duplicate codec apparatus the toolchain otherwise shuns. Browsers dismiss damaged images and fonts with no security consequence; serving them squanders bytes yet executes nothing, because no executable format stands admitted.

json_policy.facts: Text formats CSS, TXT, and CSV expose no machine-testable grammar inside this toolchain, so every candidate vets them as well-formed UTF-8 and nothing more. JSON owns an inexpensive exact grammar check in Go and Bun alike. application/json ships bare per RFC 8259, carrying no charset parameter.

ownership_scope.facts: Each project (root plus every recursive dependency directory) bears a personal manifest with a personal asset map, and graph load confinement-checks every manifest asset path. The checker can trace each calling file to its owning project. html::url values travel first-class across function and package frontiers; solely raw manifest names stand at issue.

reason_vocabulary.facts: Misshapen name literals (traversal, separators, unsafe characters) perish at check time beneath the route-literal precedent, leaving domain reasons to resolution outcomes alone. A name may live nowhere or solely inside another project. The catalogue fixes the lone str reason field and offers no message channel.
